Exact posterior predictive mean using FFBS smoothed states (MNIW model)

Source: R/func_FFBS.R
FFBS_predict_exact.Rd

Computes the analytical posterior predictive mean at new spatial locations using the smoothed state means \(s_t\) from FFBS and an exponential GP kernel for the cross-covariance.

Usage

FFBS_predict_exact(
  Y,
  para_ffbs = NULL,
  F_ls,
  F_new_ls,
  input,
  input_new,
  nT,
  phi_para,
  gp_sigma2 = 1.1,
  gp_tau2 = 10^(-4),
  delta = 1,
  theta = NULL,
  V_chol = NULL,
  residual_weights = NULL,
  return_covariance = FALSE
)

Arguments

Y

List of length nT. Observed data matrices.

para_ffbs

List. Output of FFBS, containing ff and bs.

F_ls

Covariate matrix or list for observed locations.

F_new_ls

Covariate matrix or list for new locations.

input

Numeric matrix. Coordinates of observed locations.

input_new

Numeric matrix or vector. Coordinates of new locations.

nT

Integer. Number of time steps.

phi_para

Numeric scalar. Range parameter of the exponential kernel.

gp_sigma2

Numeric scalar. Variance parameter of the GP kernel. Defaults to 1.1.

gp_tau2

Numeric scalar. Nugget variance of the GP kernel. Defaults to 1e-4.

delta

Discount factor. Not implemented: values other than 1 give a warning and are ignored. Defaults to 1.

theta

Optional list of fixed coefficient matrices, one per episode.

V_chol

Optional cached upper Cholesky factor of the input covariance.

residual_weights

Optional cached inverse-covariance-weighted residuals for the supplied coefficient trajectory.

return_covariance

If TRUE, return a list with mean and input_covariance before scaling by the emulator variance and spatial covariance.

Value

A named list of length nT. Each element "T<t>" is a matrix of dimension c(N_new, q) with the posterior predictive mean at the new locations.

See also

FFBS_predict_MC, gen_exp_kernel

Examples

set.seed(1)
dat <- gen_ffbs_data(N = 5, S = 3, p = 2, nT = 4)
par <- dat$para
res <- FFBS(dat$Y, par$F0, par$G0, par$W0, par$V0, par$m0, par$M0,
            par$n0, par$D0, nT = 4)
x_new <- matrix(c(-0.5, 0.5))  # two new inputs
pred <- FFBS_predict_exact(dat$Y, res, F_ls = par$F0,
                           F_new_ls = cbind(1, x_new), input = par$F0[, 2],
                           input_new = x_new, nT = 4, phi_para = 1)
pred$T4  # predictive mean at the new inputs (2 x S)
#>         [,1]       [,2]       [,3]
#> 6 -0.4612179 -1.5019804  0.2489372
#> 7 -0.4220251 -0.3272489 -0.1435978
